title: Subarray Sum Equals K
code:
def subarray_sum(nums, k):
    count = 0
    running = 0
    seen = {0: 1}                       # prefix sum -> how many times it occurred
    for x in nums:
        running += x
        count += seen.get(running - k, 0)     # an earlier prefix that leaves exactly k
        seen[running] = seen.get(running, 0) + 1
    return count
check:
assert subarray_sum([1, 1, 1], 2) == 2
assert subarray_sum([1, 2, 3], 3) == 2
assert subarray_sum([1, -1, 0], 0) == 3

title: Product of Array Except Self
code:
def product_except_self(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    out = [1] * n
    left = 1
    for i in range(n):
        out[i] = left                # product of everything to the left of i
        left *= nums[i]
    right = 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        out[i] *= right              # multiply by the product of everything to the right
        right *= nums[i]
    return out

title: 3Sum
Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
code:
def length_of_longest_substring(s):
    seen = set()
    left = 0
    best = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        while ch in seen:
            seen.remove(s[left])
            left += 1
        seen.add(ch)
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best

def insert(intervals, new_interval):
    result = []
    i, n = 0, len(intervals)

    while i < n and intervals[i][1] < new_interval[0]:
        result.append(intervals[i])
        i += 1

    while i < n and intervals[i][0] <= new_interval[1]:
        new_interval[0] = min(new_interval[0], intervals[i][0])
        new_interval[1] = max(new_interval[1], intervals[i][1])
        i += 1
    result.append(new_interval)

    while i < n:
        result.append(intervals[i])
        i += 1

    return result

code:
def detect_cycle(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
        if slow is fast:                 # phase 1: they meet inside the cycle
            break
    else:
        return None

    slow = head                          # phase 2: restart one pointer at the head
    while slow is not fast:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next
    return slow                          # they meet at the cycle start
check:
head = lst([3, 2, 0, -4])
tail = head
while tail.next:
    tail = tail.next
tail.next = head.next          # cycle starts at the node with value 2
assert detect_cycle(head).val == 2
assert detect_cycle(lst([1, 2, 3])) is None
assert detect_cycle(None) is None

title: Reverse Linked List II (a sublist)
code:
def reverse_between(head, left, right):
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)
    before = dummy
    for _ in range(left - 1):
        before = before.next                 # node just before the sublist
    prev, curr = None, before.next
    for _ in range(right - left + 1):
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev, curr = curr, nxt
    before.next.next = curr                  # old first node now points past the sublist
    before.next = prev                       # 'before' points to the new sublist head
    return dummy.next
check:
assert tolist(reverse_between(lst([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), 2, 4)) == [1, 4, 3, 2, 5]
assert tolist(reverse_between(lst([5]), 1, 1)) == [5]
assert tolist(reverse_between(lst([1, 2, 3]), 1, 3)) == [3, 2, 1]

title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
code:
def swap_pairs(head):
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)
    prev = dummy
    while prev.next and prev.next.next:
        first, second = prev.next, prev.next.next
        first.next = second.next           # first now skips over second
        second.next = first                # second points back to first
        prev.next = second                 # previous node points to the new front
        prev = first                       # first is now the tail of this pair
    return dummy.next
check:
assert tolist(swap_pairs(lst([1, 2, 3, 4]))) == [2, 1, 4, 3]
assert tolist(swap_pairs(lst([1, 2, 3]))) == [2, 1, 3]
assert tolist(swap_pairs(None)) == []

def largest_rectangle_area(heights):
    stack = []                                   # indices, heights increasing
    best = 0
    for i, h in enumerate(heights + [0]):        # a final 0 flushes the stack
        while stack and heights[stack[-1]] >= h:
            height = heights[stack.pop()]
            left = stack[-1] if stack else -1    # nearest smaller bar on the left
            best = max(best, height * (i - left - 1))
        stack.append(i)
    return best
check:
assert largest_rectangle_area([2, 1, 5, 6, 2, 3]) == 10
assert largest_rectangle_area([2, 4]) == 4
assert largest_rectangle_area([1]) == 1

title: Course Schedule II
template:
from collections import defaultdict, deque

def topo_order(n, edges):                  # edge (a, b): a must come before b
    graph = defaultdict(list)
    indegree = [0] * n
    for a, b in edges:
        graph[a].append(b)
        indegree[b] += 1
    queue = deque(i for i in range(n) if indegree[i] == 0)
    order = []
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        order.append(node)
        for nxt in graph[node]:
            indegree[nxt] -= 1             # one prerequisite is now satisfied
            if indegree[nxt] == 0:
                queue.append(nxt)
    return order if len(order) == n else []    # shorter means a cycle
code:
def find_order(num_courses, prerequisites):
    return topo_order(num_courses, [(pre, course) for course, pre in prerequisites])

title: Subsets
code:
def subsets(nums):
    result = []
    path = []

    def backtrack(start):
        result.append(path[:])
        for i in range(start, len(nums)):
            path.append(nums[i])
            backtrack(i + 1)
            path.pop()

    backtrack(0)
    return result

title: Sliding Window + Counting: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
code:
from collections import Counter

def character_replacement(s, k):
    counts = Counter()
    left = best = max_freq = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        counts[ch] += 1
        max_freq = max(max_freq, counts[ch])            # most common letter in the window (never lowered)
        while (right - left + 1) - max_freq > k:        # more than k letters need changing: shrink
            counts[s[left]] -= 1
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best
check:
assert character_replacement("ABAB", 2) == 4
assert character_replacement("AABABBA", 1) == 4
assert character_replacement("A", 0) == 1
